headline: Elon Musk said his companies will probably work out how to make better chips than anyone at the planned Terrafab plant, while admitting it may take years.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the headline drops Musk's own hedges ('probably', 'no idea how to make microchips' yet, 'quite a few years').
importance_line: The plan matters first to the Texas communities and workers the plant is meant to employ, then to Tesla, SpaceX and Intel, which are putting in more than US$15 billion; it is an ambition with no timetable, and Musk himself says he does not yet know how to make microchips.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by The Edge Malaysia, that Elon Musk told an X Takeover event for customers and investors, by livestream on Saturday 10 Oct, that he currently has 'no idea how to make microchips' but thinks his companies will 'probably' work out how to make them 'better than anyone', adding that it 'might take us quite a few years'. The planned Terrafab plant in Grimes, Texas, is a joint venture of Tesla, SpaceX and Intel with an initial investment of more than US$15 billion, a US$30 million Texas state grant and about 3,000 expected jobs.
notes: Bloomberg's page is closed to automated reading; the text was read on The Edge Malaysia's copy of the Bloomberg story. The url is Bloomberg's own link.
